question.text: Prior to World War II and Japanese Invasion, Indonesia was a colonial holding of this European country. This country's capital of Amsterdam is home to many speakers of the Dutch language.
question.clue: The Anti-Rent War was fought against a feudal system operated by descendents of immigrants from this country, the patroon system.

swap.leadin: Give the following about Belgian involvement in World War II.
swap.text: After the surrender of Belgium in 1940, the Belgian government evacuated from this capital city to form a government-in-exile in London.
swap.clue: This northern European capital city is sometimes called "The Capital of Europe" because it serves as the de facto capital of the European Union.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people who were murdered while praying.
question.text: A count from this region was killed by the Erembald family while praying. This region contains the cities of Bruges and Antwerp and combines with Wallonia to form a country.
question.clue: One ruler of this region was imprisoned with his two sons for attempting to ally with Edward Longshanks due to this region's prominence in the wool trade.

swap.leadin: Name some things pertaining to the many Treaties of Paris.
swap.text: The Treaty of Paris of 1783 ended the fourth war between this nation and the United Kingdom, fought over trading rights. This nation was a democracy with a stadtholder at its head.
swap.answerHtml: The Dutch Republic [accept the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands]
swap.clue: The secret Treaty of Dover caused England to start a war with this polity during the "disaster year" of 1672.

question.text: During the Eighty Years' War, this Dutch stadtholder ["shtaht-holder"] was assassinated by Balthasar Gerard, becoming the first head of state to be killed by a handgun.
question.answerHtml: William the Silent [or William I, Prince of Orange, Count of Nassau; or Willem I; or Willem de Zwijger; prompt on William of Orange]
question.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

swap.text: This Catholic nobleman led a group of like-minded politiques to ask Philip II to tolerate Protestantism in the Netherlands.
swap.answerHtml: William of Orange (accept William the Silent, prompt on William)
swap.clue: The other man of this name had his rule in Scotland legitimized by the Claim of Right and was declared king in England when the last Convention Parliament approved the Declaration of Rights.

question.text: This Belgian monarch used a military force known as the Force Publique to control his holdings in the Congo Free State and used forced labor to harvest and process rubber.
question.clue: This man formed the Force Publique to enforce his rule in a certain area, but was criticized in the Casement Report, which detailed atrocities inflicted upon rubber harvesters.

swap.leadin: When you're a naval commander and you're all out of options, there's only one thing to do: set your ships on fire and ram them into the enemy!
swap.text: Fire ships were used by the Dutch to destroy English warships during this event, during which Willem van Ghent and Michael de Ruyter led a daring attack on an English dockyard. The HMS Royal Charles was destroyed during this event.
swap.clue: During this battle, which was recorded by Samuel Pepys, George Monck sunk many of his own ships to block the enemy's progress.

question.text: Maurice and William were members of this Dutch house's Nassau branch, whose William III was installed in the Glorious Revolution. It is named for a principality rather than a color.
question.clue: Safety regulations require the use of white alternating with this color in certain tower structures, such as the Yerevan TV Tower and the Tokyo Tower.

swap.text: The oldest Jewish synagogue in the Western Hemisphere was established there in 1731, almost a century after Spain lost control of it. [10] Originally discovered by one of Columbus's lieutenants, it was declared a free port by the Dutch in 1816 after they reclaimed it from the British. [10] Today, the capital of this island in the Netherlands Antilles is Willemstad.

question.leadin: According to the book The Bookshop of the World, during this period, 10 times more books were produced per capita than in France or Spain.
question.text: Name this period, also the subject of Simon Schama's The Embarrassment of Riches. This period's end is traditionally dated to the "Disaster Year" of 1672.
question.answerHtml: Dutch Golden Age [or Gouden Eeuw; or Netherlands Golden Age; or Dutch Miracle; prompt on Golden Age]

swap.leadin: At this battle, the attacking force under Robert II of Artois was defeated by William of Julich.
swap.text: Name this 1302 battle at which French knights were decisively beaten by Flemish militia, making it an example of the nascent "Infantry Revolution."
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Golden Spurs [or Battle of Courtrai]
swap.clue: Stories of folk heroes who fought in this battle, such as the Cistercian lay brother Willem van Saeftinghe ("VILL-uhm vahn SAHF-ting-uh") and the weaver Pieter de Coninck, are romanticized in a novel by Hendrik Conscience ("kon-s'YAWNSS").

question.leadin: After this meeting, Hugo Grotius was sentenced to life imprisonment, but escaped thanks to his mistress smuggling him out of prison in a book chest.
question.text: Name this 1618 to 1619 synod in the Netherlands convened to settle the Arminian controversy. This meeting saw disputes between the Arminians and followers of Franciscus Gomarus, as well as the condemnation of Johan von Oldenbarnevelt.
question.answerHtml: Synod of Dort [or Synod of Dordt or Synod of Dordrecht]
question.clue: Moderated by Bogerman, it set forth the doctrines of perseverance of saints, irresistible grace, total depravity, limited atonement, and unconditional election.

swap.leadin: Charles II of England made this city the base for his court-in-exile.
swap.text: Name this city, whose militia murdered a French garrison in a 1302 incident known as the "Matins." An inn in this city became the world's first "bourse," giving rise to a modern word for stock exchanges.
swap.clue: The first printed book in English was printed by William Caxton in this city on the river Zwin in the Low Countries. Today, it is the capital of West Flanders.

question.leadin: This event began when attendees of Daniel Auber's opera La Muette de Portici joined Catholic rioters outside the theater doors after hearing the duet "Sacred Love of the Fatherland."
question.text: Name this 1830 event led by Charles Rogier ("roh-zhee-AY"). The Ten Days' Campaign supported by William I failed to topple a monarch installed during this event.
question.answerHtml: Belgian Revolution [or Révolution Belge; or Belgische Revolutie; or Belgische Opstand; or Belgische Omwenteling; prompt on Belgian independence]
question.clue: Sparked by perceived anti-Catholic policies, it brought to power the widower of Princess Charlotte of Wales, who later arranged the marriage of his niece Victoria to his nephew Albert.

swap.leadin: This man won the Battle of Plymouth against England while serving under Maarten Tromp.
swap.text: Name this admiral who burned thirteen English ships in an attack near Chatham that took place shortly after Holmes's Bonfire.
swap.answerHtml: Michiel de Ruyter (“mih-KHEEL duh RAO-ter”) [or Michiel Adriaanszoon de Ruyter]
swap.clue: He became friends with Frederick III of Denmark after relieving a Swedish siege of Danzig without fighting.

question.text: Following Philip II's signing of the Treaty of Joinville, Elizabeth agreed to this treaty with The Neatherlands which promised military and financial support with the goal of lifting the Siege of Antwerp.
question.clue: The Armada was assembled in response to this 1585 treaty which Elizabeth I signed. It provided English cavalry and solders to the Netherlands, and was signed in response to Philip's signing of the Treaty of Joinville.

swap.text: The strike of 1902, the second in a series of general strikes in Belgium, began when wildcat strikes broke out among miners in this province. This province faced a 1789 revolution called the Happy Revolution that restored the policies of Prince-Bishop Velbruck.
swap.clue: This so-called "Athens of the North," if by "North" you mean "Belgium," whose greatest Renaissance ruler was Erard de la Marck.

question.leadin: Name these early explorers of Australia, FTPE.
question.text: This Dutch Navigator and colonial governor became the first European to sight the coast of Australia in 1606.

swap.leadin: In the eighteenth century, emphasis placed on clinical practice and physiology led this city to surpass Padua as a center of medical learning.
swap.text: Name this city where modern medical instruction was pioneered by Herman Boerhaave. This institution's famed Hortus Botanicus was located next to an observatory built to house Rudolph Snellius's great quadrant.
swap.clue: This city celebrates Thanksgiving due to its brief role as safe harbor for the pilgrims who boarded the Mayflower, though they did so because English thugs came here to brutally assault William Brewster. It's home to a university founded in 1575 that hosted Justus Lipsius and Franciscus Gomarus.
